evidence: 0116 (records patients add themselves, text only; Akos handover step 6; owner decision 25 with D7, hide and keep); unsigned until the owner signs. Written on 0103 (34d69557); it reads nothing 0104-0115 add. REVISED AFTER TWO REVIEWS of the first draft (f9b9e5e7): notes are at most 1000 characters, as the plan's item 1a says (the draft took 2000, which no decision recorded), in the table's CHECK and in the create command; identity.has_active_membership, which the consent check behind the read policy calls, is now pinned (md5 bb52953ef1cd08527db61230a671859e, SECURITY DEFINER, STABLE, search_path identity, auth, pg_temp) in the preconditions and the post-check, with identity.has_active_consent_grant also in the post-check; the header no longer claims the withdraw command or a refresh deletes the staff chat's vectors (the command cannot: that table's forced row-level security admits only the clinician's chat transaction); ehr-api now deletes a removed record's vectors from either chunk table at that chat's next search. The ehr-api changes in the same review (no schema change): a replayed save answers 200; GET ehr/me/patient-entries?before= and the staff read page past 50 with a cursor; lengths are capped in UTF-16 units as the website counts them. BACKWARD COMPATIBLE: additive only. pg_dump --schema-only of a 0103 database before and after the runner differs only by the new table ehr.patient_entries (its primary key, unique key, index, foreign key to identity.patients, three triggers, forced row-level security, two policies and grants), three new functions (ehr.create_my_patient_entry and ehr.withdraw_my_patient_entry, SECURITY DEFINER, EXECUTE to hid_ehr_runtime and hid_schema_test_runtime; ehr.patient_entries_guard, granted to no role), their comments, and the source-kind CHECK of ehr.patient_evidence_chunks and ehr.staff_evidence_chunks, which gains patient_entry (written through NOT VALID, then validated). No existing column, row, policy, grant or function body changes. Today's EHR image reads no new object and writes only the 13 chunk kinds the wider CHECK still accepts; the new image touches the new objects only while PATIENT_ENTRIES_ENABLED is on (default off). runtime-grants.sql gains the same grants (SELECT on the table, EXECUTE on the two commands; no write grant); it is unchanged by the review. PROOFS on throwaway PostgreSQL 16 clusters (pgvector), synthetic data only, on the revised file: (1) the production chain 0001-0103 (104 files) then 0116 through the runner: plan 1 pending, dry run rolled back with 104 rows kept, applied in 87 ms, then 0 pending twice; applying the file again refuses 55000 "0116: already applied"; role bootstrap and verify pass; 78 of 78 database suites pass (77 before plus patient-entries). (2) A fresh install of 105 files: dry run, apply, 0 pending, bootstrap, verify, 78 of 78. (3) test-staging-schema-upgrade.mjs passed: baseline 104, integrated 105, declared [0116_patient_entries.sql], with production's runtime-grants.sql (sha256 594d7835...) as the baseline and again with the git-derived baseline; migrationGrantsMatchRuntimeGrants 2468, rowSecurityUnchanged 185, migrator not superuser and not BYPASSRLS. (4) Non-superuser: on 0103 copies re-owned to a NOSUPERUSER NOBYPASSRLS role, the runner applies it as that role's login and as a member login that inherits it and may SET ROLE to it, and the suite passes on both; a stranger is refused 42501 with nothing applied. (5) Refused with nothing applied (104 rows, no table): a changed platform.reject_mutation, ehr.patient_self_context, identity.has_active_consent_grant or identity.has_active_membership body (the last with its active-membership condition removed, which on the draft applied and let a clinician whose membership was deactivated read the entries), identity.has_active_membership made SECURITY INVOKER, another source-kind CHECK on either chunk table, a chunk table owned by another role, audit_platform_authority disabled; and 55P03 after about 6 s (the runner's start included) with a write held open on identity.patients or a read held open on either chunk table. (6) Locks held to commit, measured with pg_locks: SHARE ROW EXCLUSIVE on identity.patients; ACCESS EXCLUSIVE and SHARE UPDATE EXCLUSIVE on both chunk tables (last in the file); none on audit.events or any other existing table. (7) Thirteen mutants of the file each fail the suite (read policy without the active filter, no patient-self check, a two-way guard, no daily limit, no Lagos date check, created on a reused key, the staff CHECK without patient_entry, withdraw keeping the chunks, a title in the audit, a withdrawn double-tap twin replayed, and notes of 2000 in the command, in the CHECK, or in both); the unchanged file passes. The suite also runs ehr-api's vector clean-up statement in the patient's and the clinician's chat transactions: it deletes a removed entry's vectors and keeps an active entry's. Not proven here: a production-sized copy of identity.patients and of the chunk tables (the lock window grows with the chunk tables' validation, measured by the plan's study at 9 ms for 50,000 chunks).
